findings.claim: After a YouTubeEmbed instance's IFrame API load fails for video A, then succeeds for video B, then the same instance is given A again, the effect returns early at the failedVideoIdRef check while loadFailed is false, so it shows an empty player box instead of a player or the link card.
findings.impact: In collection or queue play, a rebuilt-in-place embed that returns to a video whose earlier load failed shows a blank player area and never retries, although the API loads by then. Reopening the page recovers it.
findings.evidence: YouTubeEmbed.tsx:264 `if (failedVideoIdRef.current === videoId) return;` skips setLoadFailed. Line 266 cleared loadFailed when B's effect ran, and line 380 sets failedVideoIdRef only on failure, so it still holds A. B's cleanup (lines 383-415) destroys the player and empties the host. Line 451 then renders neither the link card nor a player for A.
findings.repro: not_reproduced. Mentally: render URL_A with a rejecting loader; rerender URL_B with a working loader; rerender URL_A. No YT.Player is constructed for A and no link card is shown. EmbedLinkCard.test.tsx covers only A→B.

bucket_proposal.reason: An embed whose IFrame API load was rejected for its URL renders an empty box. I6 requires a link and says it never renders nothing.

findings.proposed_fix: In the early-return branch, call setLoadFailed(true). Alternatively, reset failedVideoIdRef when videoId changes, so a new URL retries.

findings.claim: With no metadata row, a refresh whose stored file_path hits an AmbiguousPath in resolve_on_disk raises an uncaught exception and answers 500, not the 404 'unreadable' answer.
findings.impact: The menu shows the same refreshFailed toast. It needs case-ambiguous duplicate directory names on disk.
findings.evidence: router.py:265-270 catches only (OSError, ValueError). service.py:367-373 _resolve_drive_file_path calls resolve_on_disk, which can raise AmbiguousPath (backend/app/services/diskpath.py:31 subclasses Exception directly).

specification_compliance: 188: create_loft wraps only the title fetch's exception in LoftTitleFetchError and classifies its __cause__ (unsupported first, then _classify_fetch_error). Every other exception answers 500 'failed'. The named codes are logged at info with the URL.
188 I1: create_loft_sync writes nothing before the title fetch and folder resolution, and its DB except branch unlinks the file.

188 I2/I2b: createLoft keeps only the three known string codes. linkFailureMessage maps unsupported_url and unavailable and sends everything else to the form's fallback. The subscription calls in the Composer keep their server text.

189 I4/I4b: refresh checks _require_active_file_in_drive before reading the file. It reads the file only when there is no row, checks the mime type, and requires a dict with a non-empty string url. It queues with the default stt_mode 'manual'.
190: the noCaptions texts no longer name YouTube in ja or en.
191: VimeoEmbed and YouTubeEmbed render GenericLinkCard for a missing id or a failed load. The loader removes a failed script tag. See F2 for the A→B→A gap.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A YouTubeEmbed reused for a video id whose API load failed earlier, after another URL loaded in between, renders an empty player box and makes no new load attempt.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: It needs a transient IFrame API failure followed by success while the same embed moves A→B→A in queue play; the user sees a blank player until a reload.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: rag.py now calls _has_frame_source, which reads the .loft file, for every question about a .loft video with a position, including for a profile that cannot see.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Each Ask on a .loft reads one small file from disk; nothing visible changes.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A refresh with no metadata row queues the .loft file's url as stored, without stripping it, though the emptiness check uses strip().
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Only a hand-edited .loft with surrounding whitespace in url triggers it; yt-dlp receives the padded URL.
